input.question: Which organisms have little to no role in the ecosystem?
input.ground_truth: To a certain degree, all organisms have a role in the ecosystem. Whether it's being food for a single species, or keeping predators in check, if the species is able to continue to exist in nature, it has an important role - so I'd say the ones with little to no role are the ones that are extinct (not including the ones that have been killed off, or have gone extinct due to environmental disasters). Kind of related: I've heard arguments that pandas are relatively useless in their environment? Cause they're not the sole staple diet of any one species, nor do they control prey-population sizes, but I'm open to hearing other input!

Question: Which organisms have little to no role in the ecosystem?

Let’s imagine an ecosystem is like a big playground where all the animals, plants, and tiny creatures play together. Every friend on the playground helps in some way—some help the plants grow, some eat the bugs, some clean up, and so on.

But sometimes, there are things that don’t really help or hurt the playground much. For example, if you bring a toy rock to the playground, it just sits there and doesn’t do anything. In the same way, some living things, like certain tiny bugs or plants that don’t eat, grow, or help the other animals, don’t really have a big job in the ecosystem. They are called “have little to no role,” which means they don’t help the playground work very much.
